title: Ambrosial Speech, Pure Conduct
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 266
summary: Guru Arjan strips religion down to its living core: Naam, purified conduct, saint company, worthy effort, ambrosial speech, and a heart that becomes the true place.
whyItMatters: It corrects spiritual performance, empty ritual, and language that sounds holy while conduct remains divided.
takeaway: The best religion sounds like praise and looks like clean conduct.

lines.translation: Of all religions, the best religion

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਕਰਮੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: har ko naam jap niramal karam ||
lines.translation: is to chant the Name of the Lord and maintain pure conduct.
Of all religious rituals, the most sublime ritual
is to erase the filth of the dirty mind in the Company of the Holy.
Of all efforts, the best effort

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਹੁ ਜੀਅ ਸਦਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kaa naam japahu jeea sadhaa ||
lines.translation: is to chant the Name of the Lord in the heart, forever.
Of all speech, the most ambrosial speech

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਜਸੁ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਸਨ ਬਖਾਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: har ko jas sun rasan bakhaanee ||
lines.translation: is to hear the Lord's Praise and chant it with the tongue.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਗਲ ਥਾਨ ਤੇ ਓਹੁ ਊਤਮ ਥਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sagal thaan te oh uootam thaan ||
lines.translation: Of all places, the most sublime place,

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਿਹ ਘਟਿ ਵਸੈ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੮॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: naanak jeh ghaT vasai har naam ||8||3||
lines.translation: O Nanak, is that heart in which the Name of the Lord abides. ||8||3||

structure: Ranks the path by what actually purifies rather than by outer identity.
Ties conduct, saint company, effort, and speech back to Naam.
Ends by saying the real holy place is the heart where Naam lives.
